Turbo Honda Civic Drags a Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat, and Someone Gets Thrashed After a Little Nap
7 photos
Photo: 3 Pedal Racing / YouTube
We found a new racing-related channel on YouTube, and they’re showing us a series of cool battles from the latest Streetcar Takeover event at zMax Dragway , located in Concord, North Carolina, adjacent to the Charlotte Motor Speedway.
According to the description, we are going to find here drag racing of both the quarter-mile and 1/8-mile variety, fast street and race cars, performance builds and modifications, plus race-ready action and behind-the-scenes content. However, we’re mostly interested in their coverage of the Streetcar Takeover event at zMax Dragway, of course.
The latter, alongside The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway , is among the few in the world featuring a four-lane configuration, with zMax opening in 2008 directly in the four-lane, all-concrete drag strip format, earning it the nickname "The Bellagio of Drag Strips." On this occasion, of course, only two of the four lanes are in use, though.
The video kicks off with a quick battle to set up the atmosphere between two defunct cars – a Jaguar F-Type Convertible and a Tesla Model S, dressed in classic black versus white attire. As it turns out, these two drivers were probably noobs: one of them ran a red light, possibly the Jaguar; then the Tesla darted out of its lane to try and keep up and also botched the start, but when the driver saw the red light, they slammed the brakes as hard as possible while the Jag started accelerating.
As such, the black Convertible took over the race and won the skirmish with a meager 13.08s pass while the EV came second with 13.27s. No matter, since both were in the wrong, anyway. Next up came the main event of the video – the meeting between a crimson Honda Civic hatchback of the fifth generation variety and a mighty Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat sedan.
These two clearly meant business, but again the situation was put into perspective by the importance of a good reaction time: the little Civic’s driver was subtly more precise (.150 versus .605) and took off like a storm and gained a good advantage during the early lead. It never relinquished it despite the pursuer’s higher trap speed and the “Hellcat got put to sleep by the turbo Civic” with an 11.75s versus 12.23s pass.
Today, the Honda Civic is less of a target for these bonkers aftermarket modifications, sadly. We’re also not used to seeing too many Civic Type Rs at the local quarter-mile dragstrip. The Dodge Charger fans, on the other hand, are waiting for Stellantis to get back on the V8 track with the latest iteration, which is currently only available as a Daytona EV and in Sixpack form with the 3.0-liter twin-turbo Hurricane inline-six under the hood.
